# local 0018: mcs51: conversions of volatile signed objects to wider types read the most significant byte of the object twice

- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. genCast() of ds390 also loads the most significant byte a second time, and ds390 was not compiled.
- Patch: [local-0018.patch](../../patches/local-0018.patch), commit [`8b8cd4c8f`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/8b8cd4c8fe207eef0b9294493e53ab3e80ad3add). Applies to r17228 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17228, the code for `i = v8` reads `v8` twice, and the code for `l = v16` reads the high byte
of `v16` twice. The source reads each object once.

```c
volatile signed char v8;
volatile int v16;
int i;
long l;

void s8 (void) { i = v8; }
void s16 (void) { l = v16; }
```

`sdcc -mmcs51 -S sx.c` gives `mov _i,_v8`, `mov a,_v8`, `rlc a`, `subb a,acc`, `mov (_i + 1),a`
for `s8()`. With `--model-large`, where `v8` is in xdata, `s8()` begins with `mov dptr,#_v8`,
`movx a,@dptr`, `mov r6,a`, `movx a,@dptr`, `rlc a`, `subb a,acc`. `s16()` has
`mov (_l + 1),(_v16 + 1)` and then `mov a,(_v16 + 1)` with the small model, and two
`movx a,@dptr` for the high byte with the large model.

The first read gives the low part of the result, and the second read gives the sign. When an
interrupt handler or a device changes the object from -1 to 0 between them, the result is 255.
The reads were counted in uCsim. A program reads the simulator interface at xdata 0x7f00 through
a `volatile signed char` and converts the value to `int`. The interface returns the next byte of
an answer for each read, and the conversion takes two bytes of the answer with both models.

More conversions were compiled on r17228 with earlier patches of this report, for the small,
medium, and large models and for `--stack-auto` with the small and large models. All of the
conversions of volatile signed objects in memory to wider types have the second read. This holds
for objects in `__data`, `__idata`, `__pdata`, `__xdata`, and `__code`, for objects at absolute
addresses, for local variables and parameters, and for signed `_BitInt` objects. The conversions
were from 8 bits to 16, 32, and 64 bits, from 16 to 32 bits, from 32 to 64 bits, and from `int`
to a generic pointer. The second read is present when the result is stored, returned, passed as
an argument, or used as an operand of `+=`, a multiplication, a shift, a negation, or a
comparison. Unsigned objects, reads through a pointer variable, bit-fields, conversions to
`float`, and `switch` statements on the object have one read.

## Cause

`genCast()` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` copies the bytes of the right operand to the result. For a signed
operand it then loads the most significant byte of the operand into A, with
`MOVA (opGet (right, AOP_SIZE (right) - 1, FALSE, FALSE))` below the comment "we need to extend
the sign". That load is the second read. `git blame` gives
[r617](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/617/) for the lines around it, a commit of 2001 that
changed the indentation of the source.

## Fix

For a signed right operand whose asmop has `aop_is_volatile`, the loop that copies the bytes
loads the most significant byte into A and stores A to the result, and the sign extension uses
the value in A. `aopForSym()` sets `aop_is_volatile` from the type of the symbol. For right
operands that are not volatile, `genCast()` emits the code of r17228.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/cast-volatile.c.in` is compiled four times for each port, with the
objects in `__data`, `__idata`, `__pdata`, and `__xdata`. `testValue` checks values on every port.
`testReadOnce` is for mcs51 and observes a second read with an interrupt, as `tests/critical.c`
does. The program leaves TF2 set, so the service routine of timer 2 runs after each instruction
while EA is set, and one run that the program selects changes `v8` from -1 to 0 and `v16` from
0xff55 to 0x0055. Each conversion is executed 16 times, with the change after the 1st to the 16th
instruction. Conversions that read the byte twice give 255 or 65365 when the change is between
the two reads.

On r17228 with earlier patches of this report, 24 of the 300 assertions fail for each of the six
mcs51 variants, which are the four models and `--stack-auto` with the small and large models.
With the patch, the test passes on these six, host, stm8, and ucz80. The conversion of the uCsim
program takes one byte of the answer with both models, and the conversions that were compiled for
Finding read each byte of the object once.

With the patches of this report, the regression suite has 0 failures for host, mcs51-small,
mcs51-medium, mcs51-large, mcs51-huge, mcs51-small-stack-auto, mcs51-large-stack-auto, stm8, and
ucz80, and the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80,
and stm8.

The assembly of the other regression tests differs in a conversion of a volatile `int` in
`gte/pr57131.c` and in `tests/bug3467508.c`, and in the volatile variants of `bitint`,
`bitintarith`, `muldiv`, `onebyte`, `shifts`, and `uminus`. In these variants, each difference
for mcs51-small is a store of the most significant byte from A where the code without the patch
stores it from the object. Each difference for mcs51-large is one `movx a,@dptr` that the code
with the patch does not have. The code of the tests is 293 bytes smaller for mcs51-small and 259
bytes smaller for mcs51-large, which is 1 byte for each place. The assembly files of the mcs51
libraries are identical with and without the patch for the six models.

## Related

- The entry local 0014 is about a volatile right operand of an assignment that is read again for
  each use of the value of the assignment. Its patch does not change the instructions of Finding.
- `genCast()` loads the most significant byte twice for objects that are not volatile too. With
  `--model-large`, `i = c` for a `signed char c` in xdata compiles to `movx a,@dptr`, `mov r6,a`,
  `movx a,@dptr`, `rlc a`, and the code does not need the second `movx`. The patch is limited to
  volatile operands, and the effect of the shorter sequence on other code was not measured.
- `genCast()` in `src/ds390/gen.c` has the line below "we need to extend the sign" with `aopGet`
  in place of `opGet`. ds390 was not compiled.
- `i = v8` and `l = v16` were also compiled to assembly for stm8 and z80, and the code of these
  two ports reads each object once.
